record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: Does every closed simply-connected 4-manifold admit a trisection in which one of the three 4-dimensional pieces is a 4-disk? Equivalently, is every closed simply-connected 4-manifold decomposable into three 4-dimensional handlebodies whose triple intersection is a closed surface and for which at least one of the 4-dimensional handlebodies has genus 0?

evidence.quote: As a consequence, only simply-connected 4-manifolds can admit trisections where one the 4-dimensional "pieces" is a 4-disk. Viceversa, it is an open problem whether each closed simply-connected 4-manifold admits a trisection with this property, or not: see, for example, [30], [25] and [31].

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every closed simply-connected 4-manifold admits a trisection with one piece being a 4-disk (a (g;0,*,*)-trisection) appears in recent surveys and is generally listed as an open problem in the trisection literature. No source found resolves it; existence is known for "standard" simply-connected 4-manifolds where the trisection genus equals the second Betti number, but the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Trisection Genus of Standard Simply Connected PL 4-Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Trisection genus of standard simply-connected PL 4-manifolds equals the second Betti number; achieved via simple crystallizations where pieces are 4-disks.
status_evidence.claim: Result is established only for standard simply-connected 4-manifolds, not in general.
